title: Logarithmic density saving for integer quadratics admitting unit resultant with some odd-degree integer polynomial
source_title: Solubility of a resultant equation and applications
author: Tim Browning; Stephanie Chan
difficulty_reason: A unit resultant with an unspecified odd degree does not immediately give a coefficientwise sieve restriction independent of that degree. The authors eliminate Sylvester columns and evaluate minors to extract a rational quadratic conic whose solvability forces a prime-square discriminant/nonresidue obstruction. Computing the exclusion density1/(2p) from that new reduction supplies the nonroutine arithmetic step; the precise cited large-sieve and multiplicative estimates then produce the logarithmic saving.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Counting triples (a,b,c) of absolute value at most B admitting some odd-degree R in Z[x] with resultant(R,ax²+bx+c)=plus or minus one; N(B) is at most a constant times B³/sqrt(log B). Full author resultant determinant reduction5–8 and local conic/prime-square sieve10–12 read. The new core retains odd degree as essential. Published large-sieve Lemma6.3 in reference1 and multiplicative denominator estimate reference9 TheoremA.5 are identified prerequisites. No fixed-degree class-group heuristic, imaginary-discriminant variant or almost-all common-root consequence selected. Apparent polynomial-versus-rational-function wording in Lemmas2.1/2.2 does not affect the explicitly rational conic obstruction used by the proof.

historical_source_pdf_evidence.original_difficulty_reason: The authors derive a parity-sensitive rational conic obstruction from Sylvester determinants, count excluded residue classes modulo prime squares and apply a multidimensional large sieve with a half-dimensional sieve denominator. This novel resultant-density argument exceeds ordinary qualifying-exam number theory.
